questions.question: In the assessment of adenomyosis on MRI, a "Junctional Zone" thickness of what threshold is considered diagnostic?
questions.detail: Thickening of the low-signal junctional zone on T2WI is the hallmark of adenomyosis.

questions.question: Which type of uterine fibroid (leiomyoma) is most likely to cause heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia)?
questions.detail: These involve the endometrial cavity and disrupt the normal lining.

questions.question: "Red degeneration" of a fibroid, common during pregnancy, characteristically appears on MRI as:
choices: High T1 signal rim with variable T2 signal and NO enhancement
questions.detail: This represents hemorrhagic infarction of the fibroid.

questions.question: After a first-trimester miscarriage, ultrasound shows a thickened endometrium with "intense internal Doppler flow." This is highly suggestive of:
questions.detail: The presence of blood flow helps distinguish RPOC from simple blood clots.

questions.question: Uterine "arteriovenous malformations" (AVMs) are a rare cause of life-threatening bleeding. What is the classic Doppler appearance?
questions.detail: AVMs show intense hypervascularity and "aliasing" on Doppler.

questions.question: "Endometrial carcinoma" staging is primarily based on the depth of:
questions.detail: Staging (Stage IA vs IB) depends on if the tumor invades <50% or >50% of the myometrium.

questions.question: Which MRI sequence is most important for staging endometrial and cervical cancer?
questions.detail: T2WI provides the best contrast between the tumor, the junctional zone, and the outer myometrium.

questions.question: A "T-shaped" uterus is a classic Mullerian anomaly associated with in-utero exposure to:
questions.detail: DES exposure in the 1940s–70s led to various uterine and vaginal abnormalities.

questions.question: "Septate" uterus is distinguished from "bicornuate" uterus by which feature?
choices: A normal, flat, or convex fundal contour
questions.detail: A septate uterus has a normal external shape, while a bicornuate uterus has a heart-shaped external contour.

questions.question: Why is it clinically important to distinguish a "septate" uterus from other anomalies?
choices: It is the only anomaly treated with simple hysteroscopic septal resection
it is always associated with renal agenesis
It has the lowest risk of miscarriage
questions.detail: The septum is fibrous and can be removed to improve fertility outcomes.

questions.question: "Asherman syndrome" involves the formation of intrauterine adhesions (synechiae), typically following:
questions.detail: Scarring leads to secondary amenorrhea and infertility.

questions.question: "Nabothian cysts" are benign, common findings located in the:
questions.detail: These are blocked mucus-secreting glands of the cervix.

questions.question: An "endometrial polyp" is best distinguished from a fibroid on ultrasound by its:
questions.detail: Identifying a single nutrient artery is a helpful clue for a polyp.

questions.question: "Uterine artery embolization" (UAE) is a common interventional procedure used to treat:
questions.detail: Embolizing the blood supply causes the fibroids to shrink and symptoms to resolve.

questions.question: "Pyometra" is the accumulation of pus within the uterine cavity, often secondary to:
choices: Cervical stenosis (e.g., from cancer or radiation)
questions.detail: Anything that obstructs the cervical canal can lead to fluid or pus collection in the uterus.
